purpose: Three complementary rear-campus concept views requested by Bryson. These are visual explorations, not final level layouts.
shared_prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset: a production-minded realistic environment concept for an original near-future strategy role-playing game.
Input images are references, not edit targets. Image 1 is the existing OpenBrain exterior: inherit its white panel construction, black glass bands, exact seams, stepped rectilinear masses, planted terraces, enclosed glazed bridges, friendly rounded-loop corporate emblem and restrained red access/security accents. This scene is the BACK of that same massive principal building and the much larger interconnected research park hidden behind it. Do not reproduce the front gate, creek or front-view composition. Image 2 supplies the same realistic rendering, human scale, practical cameras/readers and the guards' sports AR glasses with a physical cable to a round belt-holstered compute puck. Use those wearable details only on guards where a shot calls for them.

World: fictional California Valley/Silicon Valley/Los Angeles character, late 2030s to early 2040s, still recognizable as modern American construction and fashion. Show a very large technologically privileged private research campus, with a massive principal office/research building backed by a multi-courtyard complex of numerous distinct one-, two-, three- and five-story research/office pavilions. They belong to one cohesive architectural family; variation in footprint, height, setbacks, courtyards and function makes the park interesting. Everything is physically connected through accessible garden paths, covered walks, real stairs, ramps, lifts and glazed pedestrian bridges that join compatible levels. Ground-level exploration and walkable roof terraces are central. EACH visible roof garden has a believable access door/stair core or stair landing, walkable path and discreet safe edge railing/parapet. Buildings and bridges obey plausible perspective, structural supports, floor alignment and human proportions.

Inside aesthetic: a technological paradise and beautiful modern corporate SOLARPUNK research park. The white/black/red campus palette from the sources is preserved and enriched with healthy GREEN rooftop grass, dense planted beds, mature California trees, native-looking grasses and shrubs, maintained greenery, quiet reflective water channels and avant-garde gardens. Nature is curated, geometrically organized and sustained by systems: built-in irrigation, subtle environmental sensor nodes, water-control grilles, precise planting edges and immaculate maintenance. White architectural surfaces and black glass remain strongly readable behind the vegetation. Gardens are integrated into buildings and roofs, with clear usable paths; do not cover every facade in dangling vines. Experimental garden sections have recognizable distinct purposes and differing landscape geometry, rather than a repeated courtyard kit. This place really looks beautiful enough that a whole city built this way would be desirable.

Plausible technology is pervasive and purposeful: compact networked camera housings with smooth black optical faces at routes and access thresholds; slim white/black access readers at entrances; small plant/environment sensors; black-glass research terminals with nonverbal indicators; automatic irrigation/greenhouse controls; discreet autonomous delivery/experimental mobility equipment and docking stations; elegant photovoltaic shade canopies. Technology is integrated into the architecture and landscape, with actual cables/conduit, mounts, doors, drainage and service access where appropriate. Device status lights are tiny. Red is a sparse functional signal, not decorative strip lighting covering all edges. Outdoor research uses buildable small instruments and robotics hardware rather than mysterious glowing pylons.

People: ordinary realistic scientists, engineers and employees in familiar modern clothing, some light work jackets or occasional lab coats appropriate to the activity. They are attentive, curious, collaborative or enjoying the garden, with natural poses. They benefit from the campus but look like regular people doing their jobs; give them no villain performance, militaristic costume or worship imagery. People stay subordinate to the environment. Any security officer wears the established simple white/light-grey shirt, black trousers/shoes, small body camera and sports AR eyewear with exposed hair, a cable down the white shirt and a round black belt compute puck. Do not make every employee look like a guard.

Lighting and finish: early evening/blue hour, with enough remaining cool sky light to clearly resolve green grass, planting, rooftop routes and courtyard floor levels. Controlled warm-white occupied interiors and clean, reliable architectural/garden lighting recall the exterior reference. Keep detail readable for an artist or AI inspecting the image and for later gameplay design. Physically coherent realistic digital concept rendering, crisp perspective and materials, restrained cinematic atmosphere, no oil paint or dirty image texture. Surfaces can be mostly dry with small localized water reflections. The darkness and neglect beyond the campus perimeter may be glimpsed in the wide shot, but the park is the main subject. The troubling undertone comes from privileged abundance, comprehensive quiet observation and a maintained nature enclave surrounded by poorer places; do not turn its interior into an overtly evil prison.

Constraints: original fictional friendly rounded-loop emblems only where useful, consistent with the reference. No visible words, letters, numbers, department names, signs, labels, badges with text, road text, license-plate characters, diagram legends, screen text, real manufacturer logos or watermark. Simple pictograms/nonverbal geometry are allowed. No game interface or tile/grid overlay. No humanoid robots, AI avatars, holographic people, glowing network lines, visible scan beams, flying cars, giant mechs, elaborate armor, dystopian trash inside the campus, ruined/apocalyptic architecture, alien buildings, floating bridges or tropical fantasy jungle.
Output: one full-bleed wide landscape image, approximately 16:9; a single scene, no collage, panels, inset drawings, border or caption.

shots.title: Rear campus overview
shots.brief:
Scene and composition: a broad elevated three-quarter architectural view looking across the rear research park toward the back/side of the recognizable massive principal white-and-black stepped building. The park fills the foreground and middle distance; the principal building anchors one side/background so this clearly expands behind it. Show a large connected campus at least several city blocks in extent, with seven or more buildings of differing sizes around multiple outdoor courtyards, not merely a narrow rear patio. No giant skyscrapers. A large recognizable rear glass hall and stepped wings lead into smaller research pavilions.

Spatial organization: one clear main garden promenade connects three distinct courtyard districts. One district has geometric planted islands, shallow water rills and quiet seating among sculptural white/black shade structures. Another has a small functional autonomy-testing court/service loop beside a low research hall, with one compact white sensor-equipped electric delivery vehicle, a simple docking structure and a few small attached instruments. A third has a glass-fronted environmental/plant research pavilion, carefully tended experimental garden plots, a partial greenhouse and black-glass control posts. Each district is visibly different through landscaping, equipment and building layout, while remaining cohesive.

Rooftops: broad grass lawns and planting beds on accessible flat roofs, with visible paved walking routes, stair/lift headhouses, a few discreet solar shade canopies and plausible guardrails. A clear external stair and one glazed bridge visibly connect ground circulation to roof-level paths. Raised terraces and smaller connectors offer multiple exploration routes at different heights. Keep courtyards, entrances, stairs and bridge landings easy to trace; do not clutter or obscure them with dense foliage. Every roof garden shown must have an actual usable access point.

Life and boundaries: around six to ten small employees, distributed naturally across the large park, including two people at the outdoor experiment area and a pair on a roof path. Do not fill the image with crowds or giant foreground characters. A thin edge or distant glimpse beyond the maintained perimeter shows the darker ordinary city/dry neglected ground, making the privileged enclave legible without distracting from its beauty. Camera mounts, door readers and environmental controls appear at useful scale on the nearest routes. White, black, lush green, restrained warm light and tiny purposeful red signals. Detail priority: readable campus geography, diverse courtyard/building functions, genuine roof access and the scale of this connected technological garden.

shots.title: Experimental garden courtyard
shots.brief:
Scene: a closer human-height/low-terrace view into the experimental garden district of the SAME rear research campus. Show a large avant-garde landscaped courtyard bounded by a low glass-fronted plant/environment research pavilion, a taller three- or four-story white/black office/lab wing and a smaller service/research annex. Their green roofs have visible paths, railings and actual stair-core doors. A glazed bridge links the taller wing to a compatible level above the pavilion. One broad external stair connects the courtyard to an accessible upper planted terrace.

Garden and purpose: sculptural but plausible raised planters, deliberately arranged native-looking grasses and small trees, a shallow rill, varied geometric experimental planting beds and an adaptive louvered white/black shade canopy. Outdoor workstations have restrained equipment: attached environmental sensors, irrigation control, a small sampling/work bench, a compact sheltered terminal with nonverbal status indicators and a partial greenhouse entrance. Several carefully engineered interfaces are visible at human scale. The courtyard is beautiful, walkable and maintained, with clear paths between sections, door approaches and service access.

People: four or five small ordinary scientists/engineers in present-day trousers, shirts, simple work jackets, practical shoes; one optional light lab coat at the sampling bench. A pair discuss a tablet, one tends or observes the instrumented planting and another walks the garden path. Calm curiosity and natural interactions. One small security officer near a door wears the established sports AR eyewear with a cable to a belt puck, ordinary white/black work clothing and a body camera; do not foreground or menace the employees.

Composition: medium-wide oblique 28–35mm view at approximately human height or a shallow terrace, with the nearest sensor/planter interface inspectable, the central courtyard open and the upper route clearly visible. No giant protagonist backs. Preserve the same beautiful early-evening exposure, white/black architecture, green roofs and warm controlled lighting. Show sufficient detail to inform garden, sensor, access-reader, stair and canopy props. This is a real research garden employees enjoy and use, and a space players could explore by several connected routes.

shots.title: Green roof and research connections

Show a modest autonomy test/service lane with one compact sensor-equipped white electric vehicle and a docking/charging bay, a small instrumented observation/work bench and one small four-legged experimental field robot on a contained testing pad. The robot looks like practical near-future robotics hardware, without a weapon or humanoid form. A neighboring quieter courtyard has benches, planted geometric beds, trees and a small reflective channel. Sections have different uses led by ordinary people; they remain connected by visible garden paths and thresholds.

People and tech: two ordinary employees walk or talk on a roof path, three small researchers work or observe at the ground testing court, and one small AR-equipped security officer passes a junction. Devices are purposeful: cameras covering entrances and bridges, soil/weather sensor posts, a roof access reader, quiet docking/charging hardware and an environmental control terminal. Preserve the established device family, simple security clothing, sports AR glasses, cable and belt compute puck.

Composition: medium-wide slightly elevated viewpoint from a neighboring roof corner, roughly 28–35mm; show a readable foreground roof route leading toward the bridge, then a view down into the outdoor court. Make roof grass/planting, roof doors and reachable routes distinct enough to inform gameplay exploration.
